CausalChain: Activated CAFs -> Secretion of exosomes carrying diverse miRNA subsets -> Uptake of exosomal miRNAs by tumor cells -> miRNAs target negative regulators (e.g., SOCS proteins) and modulate IL-6 receptor isoform expression; concurrently, other miRNAs suppress tumor suppressor genes -> Upregulation and sensitization of IL-6 (and TGF-β) signaling cascades -> Enhanced activation of the JAK2/STAT3 pathway and promotion of EMT -> Increased chemoresistance and metastatic potential
Hypothesis: We hypothesize that activated CAFs release exosomes containing distinct miRNA subsets that orchestrate a multifaceted reprogramming of tumor cell signaling. Specifically, a subset of these miRNAs targets mRNAs encoding negative regulators of the IL-6 receptor (such as SOCS proteins) and shifts the balance of receptor isoforms toward those that favor robust IL-6 signal transduction. This process primes tumor cells for an exaggerated IL-6 response via the JAK2/STAT3 cascade. In parallel, additional exosomal miRNAs inhibit key tumor suppressor genes (e.g., DLC-1, GADD45A), thereby reinforcing TGF-β-driven EMT and further promoting chemoresistance and metastasis. Leveraging state-of-the-art omics technologies integrated with AI-driven analysis will facilitate the discovery and validation of these pivotal miRNA signatures. Ultimately, a dual therapeutic strategy that concurrently targets exosomal miRNA packaging/release and the dominant cytokine signaling pathways (IL-6/JAK2/STAT3 along with TGF-β) is anticipated to synergistically curb tumor progression and overcome chemoresistance.
Abstract: This study proposes that activated cancer‐associated fibroblasts (CAFs) secrete exosomes enriched with distinct microRNA (miRNA) subpopulations that concurrently modulate multiple tumor-promoting signaling pathways. One subset of these exosomal miRNAs targets mRNAs encoding negative regulators of the interleukin-6 (IL-6) receptor (for example, members of the SOCS family) and alters the alternative splicing of IL-6 receptor isoforms, thereby priming tumor cells for heightened IL-6 responsiveness. A complementary set of miRNAs targets tumor suppressor genes (e.g., DLC-1, GADD45A), reinforcing pathways such as TGF-β-induced epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT). By deploying integrated multi-omics approaches and AI-driven network analyses, we aim to precisely identify and validate these miRNA signatures. Furthermore, we propose a combinatorial therapeutic strategy that simultaneously inhibits exosomal miRNA biogenesis/release and key cytokine signaling cascades (IL-6/JAK2/STAT3 and TGF-β pathways) to synergistically attenuate EMT, chemoresistance, and metastatic progression.
Orignal_vs_New: The original hypothesis focused exclusively on CAF-derived exosomal miRNAs enhancing IL-6 responsiveness by modulating receptor isoforms and inhibiting negative regulators, leading to an amplified IL-6/JAK2/STAT3 signaling cascade. In the revised hypothesis, we have expanded the framework to integrate additional, well-supported mechanisms including TGF-β-induced EMT and direct repression of tumor suppressor genes. This update specifies potential targets (e.g., SOCS proteins for IL-6 receptor regulation, DLC-1 and GADD45A for tumor suppression) and incorporates contemporary technological capabilities such as multi-omics integration and AI-driven analyses. Furthermore, the revised model proposes a combinatorial therapeutic approach that simultaneously disrupts exosomal miRNA biogenesis and key cytokine signaling pathways, thereby addressing earlier mechanistic gaps and enhancing practical implementability.
